name: SALTO-2
question: Does laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy improve disease-specific quality of life compared with vaginal sacrospinous fixation for symptomatic post-hysterectomy vault prolapse?

design.population: Women with symptomatic post-hysterectomy vaginal vault prolapse seeking surgery at nine Dutch hospitals; 64 entered the randomized trial and 115 entered a separate treatment-preference cohort.
design.description: Multicenter randomized trial with prospective preference cohort

verdictNote: The 12-month primary comparison was nonsignificant; randomization stopped at 64 of 106 planned participants.
takeaway: Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy versus vaginal sacrospinous fixation showed no statistically significant difference in 12-month disease-specific prolapse quality-of-life scores in the 64-woman randomized SALTO-2 trial; the 115-woman preference cohort also showed no significant difference.

reports.label: 12-month randomized and cohort report
reports.citation: van Oudheusden AMJ, van IJsselmuiden MN, Menge LF, et al. Laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy versus vaginal sacrospinous fixation for vaginal vault prolapse: a randomised controlled trial and prospective cohort (SALTO-2 trial). *BJOG.* 2023;130(12):1542-1551. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.17525

results.measure: Mean 12-month UDI genital-prolapse score (0-100; lower is better), randomized trial
results.note: The trial specified a 10-point between-group difference as clinically relevant and planned to randomize 106 women; the randomized comparison was adjusted for baseline posterior-compartment stage.

results.measure: Mean 12-month UDI genital-prolapse score (0-100; lower is better), separate prospective cohort
results.note: Cohort enrollment was by treatment preference, not randomization.

results.measure: Fixed-effect mean difference in 12-month UDI score, combining randomized and preference cohorts
results.note: The combined estimate includes nonrandomized preference-cohort participants.

results.measure: 12-month apical composite success: no apical prolapse beyond hymen, bothersome bulge, repeat surgery or pessary
results.note: Adjusted odds ratio as reported in Table 3.

results.measure: 12-month apical composite success in the separate prospective cohort
results.note: Adjusted odds ratio as reported in Table 3.

results.measure: POP-Q stage 2 or higher in the anterior compartment at 12 months
results.note: Adjusted odds ratio as reported in Table 3.

results.measure: Any prolapse or non-prolapse reintervention by 12 months
results.note: The vaginal-fixation arm had three repeat laparoscopic sacrocolpopexies for apical recurrence; none occurred in the laparoscopic arm.

harms.label: Selected intraoperative complications, randomized trial
harms.locator: Results §3.1, perioperative paragraph; supplementary Table S3 cited but unavailable
harms.note: The bladder injury was recognized and repaired intraoperatively; one hemorrhage required clips and the other was managed conservatively.

harms.label: De novo dyspareunia at 12 months, randomized trial
harms.locator: Results §3.1, sexual-function paragraph; supplementary Table S1 cited but unavailable
harms.note: Percentages are among respondents with evaluable sexual-function data; denominators are not stated in the main text.

delivery.label: Technique and surgeon experience
delivery.value: Surgeons had performed at least 25 cases of each procedure. Laparoscopic repair used four ports, a Y-shaped polypropylene mesh fixed to anterior and posterior vaginal walls, sacral attachment and peritoneal closure. Vaginal repair used two nonabsorbable sutures in the right sacrospinous ligament 2 cm medial to the ischial spine.

delivery.label: Operative time, randomized trial
delivery.locator: Results §3.1, perioperative paragraph; supplementary Table S2 cited but unavailable

delivery.label: Concomitant surgery, randomized trial
delivery.locator: Results §3.1, perioperative paragraph; supplementary Table S2 cited but unavailable
delivery.note: Vaginal-group concomitant procedures were mainly anterior and posterior colporrhaphies.

relations.note: Both randomized vault-prolapse comparisons found similar patient-reported symptoms at 12 months after abdominal versus vaginal suspension.
